newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fairyoung's Pac Port IPO hotly sought.
newsitem.headline: Fairyoung's Pac Port IPO hotly sought.

text.p: Pacific Ports Co Ltd said its share offer had been 141 times subscribed, and it was raising the number of shares in the Hong Kong initial placement offer (IPO) to 60 million from 40 million.
Pacific Ports, which was spun off by Fairyoung Holdings Ltd said it had received applications for a total of 5.068 billion shares, or 141 times the number of shares available.
"We are very pleased to receive such an enthusiastic response to the company's share issue," John Chan, chairman of Pacific Ports, said in a statement.
Pacific Ports had offered 160 million shares to institutional and professional investors and 40 million for the Hong Kong IPO.
It said it was allocating 20 million shares from the international placement to the Hong Kong IPO.
The firm also granted underwriters an overallotment option to require issue of up to 30 million new shares.

After the allocation, but before any exercise of the overallotment options, Fairyoung would hold 31.94 percent of Pacific Ports, and the Asian Infrastructure Fund (AIF) would hold 32.06 percent, Pacific Ports said.
Pacific Ports said it had raised about $618 million from the issue, before exercise of the overallotment option, and deduction of expenses.

It would invest HK$180 million in its Huijian Quay project, HK$150 million for its Nanjing project, HK$60 million for its Xiangyu Quay project, HK$50 million for its Xiangyu Warehouse & Processing Zone project and HK$20 million for its Suzhou project, Pacific Ports said.
The remaining funds would be used for working capital, it said.
